summary: Submitted unchanged; validated as no_change with no effects, so no record is created or duplicated. The run ends with three research records: two sourced defects, each with an experiment-cited account whose conclusion is violated and whose defect claim is asserted, and one source-analyzed open question. Configuration recovery (98ee8dfd5fac4b84915f91ed4b094bcf-question-0) holds that with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup configuration scan, so committed configuration entries at or below it are never processed and the node keeps the snapshot's or an empty configuration; it is supported by eight retained receipts - the single-voter recovery cases with flag-off controls, the three-voter commit-rule witness reproduced in four receipts where the entry was committed and applied with only a removed server's acknowledgement while a real voter lacked it, the durable-snapshot corruption that survived a restart with the replay disabled, the authority pair with a repeat in which its premise failed and a revision that enforces it, and the two-voter vote boundary in two executions that limits the claim to candidacy rather than participation. Replay completion (29e4214f5ee146b393957fa23a33a73d-question-0) holds that the startup replay blocks forever once it needs more than 128 delivered batches, because the FSM channel's only consumer is started after the replay returns and the send has no timeout; it is supported by eleven receipts covering the block pair, the measured bound pair, the availability consequence at two batch sizes, the exact 128-versus-129 delivered-batch boundary at two batch sizes with the bound stated as 128 x MaxAppendEntries, and reachability with the library's default snapshot settings. Three knowledge corrections (tuple-counted batching, the randomized snapshot cadence, and the enumerated writers of the tracked configuration) are recorded with changed premises, affected uses marked and gaps answered; 54 claims across 14 receipts were verified against the observations with no discrepancy and the cited source anchors re-checked; one internal contradiction was repaired; the predecessor receipt that failed inside its own harness is retained without a comparison claim. The open question dec7dd4ba25743138e52303340152c0c-question-0 records, with source analysis, the two readings of whether a stale snapshot's configuration can reach a joiner through InstallSnapshot - including the concrete persistent path in which a stale-configuration leader takes a further snapshot so that the corrective entry lies below the new snapshot index - and carries a discriminator but no execution. Remaining limits are structural (in-memory transports and stores in one process, no production store, no process-level restart or disk fault, one prefix shape per scenario), and expiry preserves this state.
